Example SEO page

This fixture exists so the audit has a page with the elements a public page should have. It has a title, a description, a canonical URL, one H1, structured data, internal links and a reasonable amount of text.

The audit is deliberately blunt: it checks whether the page can be indexed, whether the metadata is present and sane, whether the content is thick enough to compete, and whether an AI agent can discover a markdown version and an llms.txt summary.

None of these checks guarantees a ranking. They are the floor, not the ceiling. A page still needs a reason to exist: original data, a tool, a real comparison, a named author, or a point of view that is not already on the first page of results.

This paragraph is here to push the word count over three hundred so the fixture does not trigger the thin-content warning. The text is intentionally repetitive but readable, because a fixture should fail only the checks it is designed to fail.

Read the docs for the reasoning behind each check, and use the audit as a starting point rather than a score to optimise. A green audit on a page nobody wants is still a page nobody wants.
